title: Insular art
description: Post-Roman British and Irish style of art
extract: Insular art, also known as Hiberno-Saxon art, was produced in the post-Roman era of Great Britain and Ireland. The term derives from insula, the Latin term for "island," as in this period Britain and Ireland shared a largely common style different from that of the rest of Europe. Insular art is usually classified as early medieval art, and sometimes more specifically as Migration Period art. It is the combination of these two traditions that gives the style its special character.
